correctness.rationale: PASS: The Kripke clauses yield Diamond A={S:S intersect P(A) nonempty} and Box A={S:S intersect Q(A) empty}, where P and Q union the members of A and its complement; singleton worlds recover P,Q from the output. Every singleton belongs to exactly one family, so P union Q=U. If both were proper, choosing i outside P and j outside Q and examining world {i,j} is contradictory, hence P=U or Q=U. Each proper support requires a covering family of nonempty subsets of S and has H(|S|) realizations by inclusion-exclusion. For n>=2 A={U} realizes (U,U); n=1 is exceptional. Disjoint counting gives central count. The p=n-1 term dominates H(p) asymptotically, yielding exactly 2n*2^(-2^(n-1)) for noncentral probability. The independent script directly traversed Kripke edges for all 2,8,128,32768 valuations at n=1..4, producing output counts 2,7,15,31 and central masses 0,2,90,31826. Finite enumeration corroborates, but does not replace, the arbitrary-n proof.

final_claim: For each n>=2, on W_n=P([n]) without the empty state and with accessibility nonempty intersection, the unrestricted one-step map A -> (Diamond A, Box A) has exactly 2^(n+1)-1 labelled outputs; every proper support pair (S,[n]) or ([n],S) has H(|S|) preimages, H(p)=sum_j(-1)^j binom(p,j)2^(2^(p-j)-1), and the central output (W_n, empty) has 2^(2^n-1)-2 sum_{p<n} binom(n,p)H(p) preimages. A uniform random A gives a noncentral output with probability asymptotic to 2n*2^(-2^(n-1)). For n=1 exactly two outputs and no central fiber.
limitations: The input distribution is uniform over unrestricted Kripke propositions, not the parameter-free forcing semantics of the motivating paper.
Exact results are one-step only and n=1 is exceptional; no deeper modal-fragment classification is claimed.
